## Frozen commentary (Turkish)

İnsanlar kendilerini bir köke bağlar, soylu ya da düşük. Asr kökü bu soyun adıdır: {ar:العنصر والعنصر الأصل والحسب, tr:el-unsur, gloss:unsur, kök ve soydur, source:"ع ص ر,B011"}, {ar:فلان كريم العصير أي كريم النسب, tr:kerîmu'l-asîr, gloss:soyu temiz, source:"ع ص ر,B011"}; aynı kök azatlıların en düşüğünü de adlandırır: {ar:هؤلاء موالينا عصرة أي دنية دون من سواهم, tr:mevâlînâ usratan, gloss:bunlar bizim en alt derecedeki azatlılarımız, source:"ع ص ر,B012"}. Kayıp kelimesinin uzatılmış biçimleri de insanların zayıflarını ve bayağılarını anlatır: {ar:الخناسر الضعاف من الناس, tr:el-hanâsir, gloss:hanâsir, insanların zayıflarıdır, source:"خ س ر,B005"}. Karşısında insan, türün bütünüdür: {ar:الإنس البشر, tr:el-insu'l-beşer, gloss:ins, insan türüdür, source:"ء ن س,B001"}.

Birinci ayetin kelimesi soyu ve rütbeyi çağrıştırırken, ikinci ayet istisnasız "insan" der: kayıp soylu ile düşüğü birlikte kapsar. Ayrımı üçüncü ayet yapar ve onu soya değil, imana ve işe bağlar. Düz anlatım bu eşitlemenin, soy ve rütbe adını taşıyan bir kelimenin hemen ardından geldiğini fark ettirmez. Kur'an soyların kesildiği anı kayıpla birleştirir: {ar:فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَلَآ أَنسَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ, tr:fe-izâ nufiha fi's-sûri fe-lâ ensâbe beynehum yevmeizin, gloss:sûra üflendiğinde o gün aralarında soy bağı kalmaz, source:23:101}, iki ayet sonra kendini kaybedenler gelir {source:23:103}. Üstünlük ölçüsü de açıkça değiştirilir: {ar:إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ, tr:inne ekramekum indallâhi etkâkum, gloss:Allah katında en değerliniz, en çok sakınanınızdır, source:49:13}. Nuh'un kavminin ileri gelenleri ise imanı rütbeyle ölçer: {ar:قَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَٱتَّبَعَكَ ٱلْأَرْذَلُونَ, tr:kâlû enu'minu leke vettebeake'l-erzelûn, gloss:sana en aşağılıklar uymuşken biz mi sana inanacağız dediler, source:26:111}; bir başka anlatımda {ar:وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا, tr:ve mâ nerâke'ttebeake illellezîne hum erâzilunâ, gloss:sana ancak aramızdaki en düşüklerin uyduğunu görüyoruz, source:11:27}.

const r = await tools.exec_command({
  cmd: `cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec14/luna/list.tsv <<'EOF'
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.49.3\tlow/high and rich/poor together\tThe commentary says al-insan includes noble and low; this psalm explicitly addresses low and high, rich and poor together before warning against confidence in wealth, making its wisdom socially comprehensive.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.62.10\thigh and low weighed alike\tThe commentary places noble and lowest ranks inside one loss; this verse says low-born are vanity and high-born a lie, together lighter than breath on the scales, turning rank into shared futility.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Job.34.19\tGod shows no partiality to princes or rich\tThe commentary makes lineage and rank irrelevant to humanity's loss; Job describes the Creator as neither favoring princes nor preferring rich over poor, grounding equal standing in God's making of all.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Lev.19.15\tneither poor nor great favored in judgment\tThe commentary relocates distinction from birth rank to faith and conduct; this law forbids favoring the poor or deferring to the great and requires just judgment, making status irrelevant to assessment.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ezek.18.20\tindividual guilt, not a father's\tThe commentary refuses inherited lineage as a criterion; Ezekiel says a son does not bear his father's guilt and each person bears his own, making accountability individual rather than genealogical.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ezek.18.21\trepentance and practiced justice\tWhere the note says the surah distinguishes by faith and deeds, Ezekiel says a wicked person who turns and practices justice and righteousness will live, making changed conduct rather than parentage decisive.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Mal.3.18\trighteousness and service\tThe note says the third ayah distinguishes by faith and work; Malachi's promised distinction is between righteous and wicked, and between one who serves God and one who does not, an ethical-religious axis rather than lineage.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tMishnah Sanhedrin 4:5\tone Adam; no superior ancestry\tThe commentary breaks lineage's status claim by including noble and low alike; the Mishnah says Adam was created singly so none can boast that their ancestor is greater, an explicit rabbinic rejection of pedigree ranking.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWisdom of Solomon 6:5\tjudgment falls severely on rulers\tThe commentary places high and low within the same human loss; Wisdom warns that judgment falls severely on those in high office, showing that rank increases exposure rather than offering shelter.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWisdom of Solomon 5:8\twealth and boasting fail at judgment\tThe commentary brings rank and loss together; in the wicked person's postmortem confession, Wisdom asks what wealth and arrogance profited them, exposing status as no protection at judgment.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tSirach 10:14\trulers overturned, humble raised\tThe commentary names both high rank and the lowest social position; Sirach says God overturns rulers' thrones and installs the lowly, making earthly rank reversible under divine judgment.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.3.8\tfruit worthy of repentance\tThe commentary says the surah's distinction is made by faith and deeds; John demands conduct that bears fruit worthy of repentance, setting an ethical test beside the following rejection of inherited confidence.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.3.9\tAbrahamic descent cannot secure standing\tThe commentary rejects lineage as the basis of distinction; John warns hearers not to rely on Abraham as father and says God can raise children for Abraham from stones, denying inherited pedigree as a guarantee.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:John.8.39\tAbraham's children must do Abraham's works\tThe commentary says rank by descent gives way to faith and action; Jesus answers a claim of Abrahamic descent by making Abraham-like deeds the test of true kinship.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.2.6\tjudgment according to deeds\tThe commentary assigns distinction to belief and righteous work rather than lineage; Paul says God repays each according to deeds, giving the same non-hereditary measure in a judgment setting.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.2.11\tGod shows no partiality\tThe note's human category includes high and low without exception; Paul says God shows no partiality in judgment, removing social or inherited standing as an advantage.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Pet.1.17\timpartial judgment of each person's work\tThe commentary says lineage does not decide who is lost and deeds mark the distinction; Peter describes the Father as judging each person's work impartially, closely joining both claims.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Acts.10.34\tGod shows no partiality\tThe commentary includes high and low in the same human category; after Peter's vision opens the message to Gentiles, he says God shows no partiality, removing inherited peoplehood as a barrier.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Acts.10.35\tfear of God and right action across nations\tThe commentary makes faith and deeds the dividing criterion; Peter says a person from any nation who fears God and does what is right is acceptable, explicitly replacing ancestry with religious conduct.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:James.2.2\trings and clothing mark social rank\tThe commentary names noble descent and the lowest freedmen; James's assembly scene distinguishes a gold-ringed, finely dressed visitor from a poor person in shabby clothes, making rank's visible signs concrete.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:James.2.3\tpreferential seating for the rich\tThe note says status should not decide human worth; James depicts the rich being offered a good seat while the poor are made to stand or sit below, then condemns the community's class judgment.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:James.2.5\tpoor rich in faith and heirs\tThe commentary says the later ayah distinguishes by faith and work; James says God chose the poor to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, reversing social rank through faith.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:James.2.9\tpartiality is sin\tThe commentary replaces inherited rank with a religious-ethical criterion; James explicitly calls favoritism toward status groups sin, giving the social hierarchy a moral verdict.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Cor.1.26\tnoble birth among the called\tThe commentary contrasts lineage and rank with the surah's criterion of faith and deeds; Paul reminds the Corinthians that few were wise, powerful, or well-born when called, showing the community was not selected by elite status.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Cor.1.27\tGod chooses the weak\tThe note includes the lowest ranks within humanity; Paul says God chose the world's weak and foolish to shame the strong and wise, reversing the social measure of worth.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Cor.1.28\tlowly and despised chosen\tThe commentary highlights the lowliest freedmen and weak people; Paul says God chose what is low and despised, even what is not, to nullify what is, directly reversing status.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Cor.1.29\tno human may boast before God\tThe commentary removes lineage as a basis for superiority; Paul says God's choice leaves no human able to boast before God, explicitly closing off inherited or social prestige.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Gal.3.28\tJew/Greek and slave/free made one\tThe commentary says al-insan includes noble and low alike; Paul names Jew/Greek and slave/free distinctions and says they do not divide those in Christ, shifting standing away from inherited and social categories.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.12.20\trich man's death defeats his security\tThe commentary pairs rank with human loss; God tells the rich landowner his life is required that night, so accumulated wealth and status cannot secure him from death.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.12.21\trich toward God\tThe commentary says the final distinction is not lineage but faith and deeds; Jesus applies the rich fool's story to one who stores treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.16.22\tboth die; poor man exalted\tThe commentary includes the high and low in humanity's loss; Luke has both Lazarus and the rich man die, but Lazarus is carried to Abraham's side while the rich man is buried, reversing earthly rank.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.16.25\tlife's status reversed after death\tThe note says rank cannot determine the final distinction; Abraham tells the rich man that he received good things in life while Lazarus received bad, but now Lazarus is comforted and he is in anguish.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rev.20.12\tgreat and small judged by deeds\tThe commentary says no human rank escapes the encompassing judgment and deeds distinguish; Revelation pictures the dead, great and small, before the throne and says they are judged by what they did.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.1.52\trulers brought down, humble exalted\tThe commentary sets lineage and high/low rank beside universal human loss; Mary's praise says God brings rulers from thrones and exalts the lowly, a direct reversal of social rank.
medium\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Prov.22.2\tone Maker of rich and poor\tThe commentary's al-insan embraces noble and low; Proverbs says rich and poor meet because the Lord made them both, grounding their common humanity in one Creator.
medium\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.49.18\twealth does not follow at death\tThe commentary places status and loss in adjacent ayat; the psalm says a dying rich person carries nothing away and his glory does not descend with him, concretizing why wealth cannot secure the human.
medium\ttevrat\tkarsi_anlati\tWLC:Eccl.9.2\tthe same earthly fate for righteous and wicked\tThe commentary says humanity is in loss while the next ayah marks a believing, righteous exception; Qoheleth says the same fate comes to righteous and wicked, clean and unclean, in the earthly register of death, sharpening the difference in horizon.
medium\ttevrat\tparalel\tWLC:Gen.6.9\tNoah righteous amid a corrupt generation\tThe commentary's Noah scene says elites reject him because low-status people follow; Genesis presents Noah as righteous and blameless amid a corrupt generation, framing the same figure through his conduct without mentioning follower rank.
medium\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:1Sam.16.7\theart over stature and appearance\tSamuel initially sees Eliab's stature as kingly, but God says he sees the heart rather than appearance; this parallels the commentary's move away from rank toward an inner moral criterion.
medium\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Isa.40.23\tprinces reduced to nothing\tWhere the commentary says noble and low ranks share human loss, Isaiah says God reduces princes to nothing and makes rulers as emptiness, portraying status as unable to endure before God.
medium\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Job.14.1\tArabic ء ن س and Hebrew אנוש; table correspondence, BDB notes Arabic cognate\tThe commentary uses insan for humanity and says no rank escapes loss; Job calls אנוש, the human born of woman, few of days and full of trouble, a direct mortal-human use of the table's Arabic-linked Hebrew root.

strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:1Sam.2.7\tGod reverses poor and rich\tThe commentary places noble and lowest ranks inside one human loss; Hannah's song says YHWH makes poor and rich and brings low and high down or up, making rank reversible under divine sovereignty.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:1Sam.2.8\tpoor raised to sit with princes\tThe commentary names the lowest social ranks; Hannah's song says God raises the poor from dust and seats the needy with princes, directly overturning the status scale used by Noah's accusers.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.113.7\tpoor lifted from dust in Hallel\tThe commentary recalls the lowest freedmen; this Hallel praise celebrates YHWH lifting the poor from dust and the needy from the ash heap, turning rank reversal into communal liturgy.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.113.8\tneedy seated with princes\tThe next verse says the needy are seated with princes; it gives the commentary's high/low contrast a liturgical image of the low receiving the highest social seat.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Exod.30.15\tequal half-shekel for rich and poor\tThe census ransom is one half-shekel per person: the rich may not give more and the poor less. This Torah rule gives the commentary's inclusion of high and low a concrete equal measure.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Jer.9.22\tno boasting in wisdom, might, or wealth\tThe commentary treats lineage and rank as human status measures; Jeremiah forbids boasting in wisdom, strength, or riches, showing that several forms of social capital cannot secure standing.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Jer.9.23\tboast in knowing the God who does justice\tJeremiah redirects boasting to understanding and knowing YHWH, who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness; this specifies the commentary's shift from lineage to religious and ethical standing.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Zeph.3.11\thaughty removed from God's mountain\tThe commentary says high rank cannot exempt anyone from loss; Zephaniah says God will remove the haughty from the holy mountain on the day of judgment, directly lowering status before God.
strong\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Zeph.3.12\thumble remnant seeks refuge in YHWH\tThe commentary makes the distinction by faith and deeds; Zephaniah leaves a humble, lowly people who seek refuge in YHWH's name, joining low status to trust rather than pedigree.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.11.17\twild branches share the cultivated root\tThe commentary calls the root an image of lineage; Paul pictures Gentile believers grafted into Israel's olive tree to share its root, giving the lineage image a specific scene of inclusion across peoples.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.11.18\troot supports branches, so do not boast\tThe commentary describes people grounding superiority in lineage; Paul tells the grafted branch not to boast over natural branches because the root supports it, explicitly overturning pedigree pride.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.11.20\tstanding by faith, not inherited branch status\tThe commentary says distinction turns on faith rather than lineage; Paul says natural branches were broken off through unbelief while Gentile branches stand through faith, then warns against pride.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.9.6\tdescent from Israel is not sufficient\tThe commentary denies that lineage determines the human verdict; Paul says not all descended from Israel belong to Israel, distinguishing physical descent from covenant standing.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.9.8\tchildren of promise, not flesh alone\tPaul explains that children of the flesh are not thereby God's children and that children of promise count as offspring; this gives the commentary's lineage/status issue a specific theological redefinition.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.2.28\toutward identity does not decide standing\tThe commentary says inherited rank is not the criterion; Paul says Jewish identity and circumcision are not merely outward or bodily, challenging status carried by visible ancestry markers.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.2.29\tinward identity and praise from God\tPaul defines the true identity by circumcision of the heart through the Spirit and praise from God, giving the commentary's move from lineage to inward religious standing a specific formulation.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:John.1.12\tbelievers become children of God\tThe commentary says lineage does not decide who belongs among the saved; John says those who receive and believe in Jesus' name are given the status of God's children.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:John.1.13\tbirth not from blood but from God\tJohn specifies that God's children are not born from blood or human will but from God, directly denying natural descent as the source of religious standing.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.21.31\toutcasts enter before religious leaders\tIn Jesus' temple dispute, he says tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God's kingdom ahead of the leaders; this closely matches the commentary's picture of elites discrediting a prophet because low-status people follow him.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.21.32\tbelief and repentance distinguish the groups\tJesus explains that the outcasts believed John while the leaders did not repent after seeing it; this makes response to the message, not public rank, the reason for their different standing.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Luke.18.14\ttax collector justified over Pharisee\tIn the paired prayer scene, Jesus says the tax collector goes home justified rather than the Pharisee; the religiously prestigious figure does not outrank the despised man who humbles himself before God.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.20.26\tgreatness defined as service\tThe commentary names inherited and social rank, then says deeds mark distinction; Jesus says the one who wants to be great must become a servant, replacing status with conduct.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Matt.20.27\tfirst place defined as slavery to all\tJesus continues that the one who wants to be first must become a slave to all, directly reversing the rank logic behind the commentary's noble and lowest social categories.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Cor.12.22\tweaker parts are indispensable\tThe commentary notes that low and weak people remain within the human category; Paul says body parts that seem weaker are indispensable, giving low status a necessary role in the community.
strong\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:1Cor.12.23\tless honorable parts receive greater honor\tPaul says the body's less honorable parts are treated with greater honor; this is a concrete reversal of rank within the community, not merely a claim that all parts exist.
strong\tincil\tkarsi_anlati\tSBLGNT:Eph.2.8\tsalvation as gift through faith\tThe commentary says the final distinction is by faith and deeds; Ephesians says salvation comes by grace through faith as God's gift, locating its source in grace and faith rather than human achievement.
strong\tincil\tkarsi_anlati\tSBLGNT:Eph.2.9\tworks are not the basis for boasting\tEphesians says salvation is not from works so that no one may boast, a specific difference from the commentary's formulation that righteous deeds help distinguish the saved.
medium\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Ps.8.5\tArabic ء ن س and Hebrew אנוש; table correspondence, BDB notes Arabic cognate\tThe commentary uses insan for the whole human species; Psalm 8 uses אנוש for the human being whom God remembers and crowns with glory and honor, a direct human-term correspondence with a strikingly dignified context.
medium\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Ps.8.5\thumanity crowned with glory and given dominion\tThe commentary says all humanity is in loss regardless of rank; Psalm 8 depicts the human being as remembered, crowned with glory, and given dominion, adding a distinct account of dignity bestowed by God.
medium\ttevrat\tsoydas\tWLC:Exod.16.18\tArabic خ س ر and Hebrew חסר; table sound correspondence, unverified\tThe commentary says high and low are included in khusr; at manna gathering, those who gather much have no surplus and those who gather little do not חסר, giving the table's unverified root match a specific scene of equal sufficiency.
medium\ttevrat\tmotif\tWLC:Mal.2.10\tone father and Creator, shared obligation\tMalachi asks whether the community has one father and one Creator, then asks why its members betray one another; it connects common origin to ethical duty, while its immediate scope is covenant Israel rather than all humanity.
medium\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Acts.17.26\tall nations from one ancestor\tThe commentary pairs lineage with the universal human category; Paul says God made every nation from one ancestor and appointed their times and boundaries, giving common human origin a concrete biblical formulation.
medium\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Acts.17.27\tall peoples directed to seek God\tPaul continues that the nations' situation is ordered so they might seek God; this adds a shared religious task to the common ancestry in the preceding verse.
medium\tincil\tkarsi_anlati\tSBLGNT:Eph.2.10\tgood works as the result of grace\tThe preceding verses deny that works earn salvation, but Ephesians says believers are created in Christ for good works; this preserves a role for deeds while locating them as the result, not the basis, of salvation.
medium\ttevrat\tsoydas\tSanhedrin 37a\tAdam's seal and each person's uniqueness\tThe Mishnah's single Adam is expanded: humanity bears one divine seal, yet no person resembles another and each must regard the world as created for them. This adds individual worth to the commentary's inclusion of every rank.
medium\tincil\tyorum_gelenegi\t1 Clement 13:1\tChristian reception of Jeremiah's anti-boasting formula\tClement applies Jeremiah's warning against boasting in wisdom, strength, and wealth to Christian humility, giving an early Christian interpretation of the status critique in Jeremiah 9.
medium\tincil\tmotif\tDidache 4:3\timpartial correction and just judgment\tThe church rule commands just judgment and no partiality when correcting transgressions; it gives the commentary's move from rank to religious conduct a concrete communal practice.
medium\tincil\tmotif\tSBLGNT:Rom.12.16\tassociate with the lowly, do not be haughty\tPaul tells the community not to be proud and to associate with the lowly; the Greek can also mean associating with humble things, so this is a specific but textually ambiguous answer to elite distance from low-status people.
